statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 10% (low). NQZ26 prints 31,041.75 at 06:59:35Z, -0.06% against a 31,061.75 prior close, after a third successive lower low at 31,003.75 was bought back by about 38 points. The 31,221.25 high has stood unretested for more than five hours and the full session range is 0.70%. The 06:10Z rally to 31,071.25 failed before that low, but recovery depth is improving across the sequence, from about 20 to about 38 points. ES -0.10% and YM -0.04% confirm trivial cross-index magnitude. Stress eases to 53% (elevated) as WTI 90.07 resumes a 1.14% fade and Brent 101.76 slips 0.48%, against a 10-year yield confirmed higher at about 5.29% on 2 October. Confidence 88% (high) on a verified five-minute intraday price path.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours with a 7% floor and a 13% peak. The narrow danger window spans 13:00-15:00Z on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and September ISM Services at 14:00Z. That window is published on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: Tail ticks to 10% as a third lower low at 31,003.75 is bought back by 38 points inside a 0.70% range, with ES -0.10% and YM -0.04% confirming trivial magnitude and Stress easing to 53% on a resumed crude fade
body:
A third successive lower low printed overnight and scoring that sequence honestly, without over-reading it, is the work of this hour. NQZ26 prints 31,041.75 at 06:59:35Z against a 31,061.75 prior close, a decline of 20.00 points or 0.06%. The session low is no longer 31,036.75; a fresh 31,003.75 low printed during this hour, the third lower low in three hours after 31,059.00 and 31,036.75. The session range is therefore 31,003.75 to 31,221.25, a span of 217.5 points or 0.70%, and the 31,221.25 high has now stood unretested for more than five hours.

The five-minute path is the decisive evidence, and it cuts both ways. Price rose to 31,071.25 at 06:10Z, failed there, and then slid to 31,013.00 by 06:40Z before basing and recovering to 31,040.00 at 06:55Z. That is a failed retracement followed by a fresh extension, which the contract names as an amplifier. Against it, the recovery off this low measures roughly 38 points, against roughly 20 points off the previous low an hour earlier. The depth of the bounces is increasing, not decreasing, and the 31,000 round level held on the first test. A sequence of lower lows in which each low is bought more aggressively than the last is a widening two-way range with a downward drift, not a path that denies mean reversion.

Tail therefore rises from 8% to 10%, mapping to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The two points recognise a genuine structural fact: three lower lows and a high unretested for five hours mean the overnight path is no longer the completed round-trip described two hours ago. The increase stops at two points because the magnitude is trivial and the retracement evidence is improving. A complex in which the index future is down 0.06%, ES is down 0.10% and YM is down 0.04% is not producing directional efficiency. Holding 8% would ignore the lower-low sequence; moving materially higher would mistake a 0.70% overnight range for a pathological path.

The cross-asset picture remains directionally aligned and immaterial in size. ES trades 7,769.50, down 7.75 or 0.10%, inside a 7,764.00 to 7,793.00 range that spans 0.37%. YM trades 51,456.00, down 21.00 or 0.04%, inside 51,377.00 to 51,560.00. All three index futures are mildly negative, which is alignment of a kind, but alignment at four to ten basis points is not an amplifier. The absence of any single index leading the others lower is itself evidence against a developing impulse.

Stress eases one point to 53% because the energy complex has resumed the fade that paused an hour ago. WTI trades 90.073, down 1.04 or 1.14%, and Brent trades 101.761, down 0.49 or 0.48%. Crude is the live component of this environment while cash yields are closed, and it is cooling rather than firming. The backdrop nonetheless stays genuinely difficult and keeps Stress elevated: Brent above 100, a Strait of Hormuz closure now past Day 219 with flows described as structurally impaired, a 10-year yield confirmed to have reversed higher to 5.2939% on 2 October rather than falling on weak jobs data, and a September employment report that produced 29,000 payrolls against roughly 90,000 expected, an August revision down to 133,000 from 162,000, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings up 0.1% to 37.81 dollars. Stress does not fall further because none of those has resolved, and it does not rise because nothing new has deteriorated.

Confidence improves one point to 88%, which remains high. The evidence set is denser than an hour ago in one specific and important way: this assessment holds the actual five-minute intraday price path from the Yahoo Finance chart series, timestamped to 06:59:35Z, rather than only a point quote. That is what allows the failed 31,071.25 retracement and the improving bounce depth to be stated as observations instead of inferences. Alongside it sit live ES and YM prints stamped to 06:59:37Z and 06:59:31Z, the primary BLS employment release, the verified 2 October Americas market wrap that resolved the yield direction, the H.15 yield series, and current crude quotes. The honest limits are specific and unchanged in character. Cash VIX and cash Treasuries are closed, so the 15.31 VIX reading is a 2 October close rather than a live level, and H.15 last published 4.78% at two years and 5.24% at ten years for 1 October, a session behind the market. The Investing.com quote carried an explicit delayed-data label and a 02:18 stamp that predates the Yahoo print, so it was used only to corroborate the 31,021 area low and not as a current reference; reconciling the two feeds by timestamp is what revealed the intrahour recovery and subsequent slide. Barchart returned an empty payload and the CNBC week-ahead article returned HTTP 403, both site-side bot blocks rather than egress failures, and neither was relied upon. The shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection timestamp, roughly 8,990 minutes old, with a partial collection status and recorded calendar and futures adapter failures, so it was treated as unusable under the inherited freshness rule and this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

The published path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. It carries 10% through the European cash-open hour, eases to 9% and then to an 8% floor as European trade is assumed to mature into two-way conditions, ticks back to 9% for the 12:00Z US pre-market build, and rises to 12% and a 13% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the 13:30Z cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and September ISM Services at 14:00Z. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not claims about structure that cannot yet be observed. The path then decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 10% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to a 7% floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt, and runs an 8% to 9% band through the Asian session and the European pre-open on 6 October.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history, and every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The 06:00Z slot on 5 October is explicitly unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock-hour; its fields are null rather than interpolated. Tail was held at 3% from 07:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. It then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended: 12% at 22:00Z, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once the fresh 31,221.25 high failed, to 10% at 03:00Z as the retracement completed through the prior close, and to 8% at 04:00Z and 05:00Z as that round-trip appeared to hold. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through 73%, 70%, 68% and 66% into a 64% trough at 14:00Z as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and then settled through 66%, 65%, 64%, 62%, 60%, 57% and 54% across the reopen hours. Confidence held a narrow 83% to 88% band, densest in the European and early US hours and thinnest across the weekend halt and the earliest reopen hours.
